arrays.summary: Foundation of DSA. Master traversal, prefix sums, two pointers, and hashing-based lookups before moving on.

strings.summary: String manipulation, anagram detection, substring problems, and sliding window on character arrays.

hashing.summary: O(1) average lookup with hash maps and sets. Used in counting, grouping, and existence queries.

two-pointers.summary: Opposite-end and same-direction pointer techniques on sorted arrays and linked lists.

sliding-window.summary: Maintain a window of elements with O(n) complexity. Fixed-size and variable-size variants.

prefix-sum.summary: Precompute cumulative sums to answer range queries in O(1). Extends to 2D and difference arrays.

binary-search.summary: Halve the search space every step. Classic sorted-array search plus search-on-answer for optimization problems.

linked-list.summary: Pointer manipulation without random access. Fast/slow pointer detects cycles; reversal is a core technique.

stacks-queues.summary: LIFO/FIFO structures. Monotonic stack solves next-greater-element; deque enables O(n) sliding-window max.

recursion.summary: Express a problem in terms of smaller subproblems. Base case + recurrence. Merge sort is the archetype.

backtracking.summary: Pruned exhaustive search. Choose–Explore–Unchoose. Used for permutations, combinations, and constraint satisfaction.

trees.summary: Recursive structure. DFS (pre/in/post order) and BFS (level order). Path problems and LCA are essential.

bst.summary: In-order traversal of a BST yields sorted sequence. Master insert, delete, validate, and kth-smallest.

heap.summary: Efficient min/max extraction. Used for top-K elements, k-way merge, and scheduling.

greedy.summary: Make the locally optimal choice at each step. Prove correctness with exchange argument or counterexample.

dynamic-programming.summary: Overlapping subproblems + optimal substructure. Top-down (memoization) or bottom-up (tabulation).

graphs.summary: BFS/DFS on general graphs. Topological sort for DAGs, Dijkstra for SSSP, Union-Find for connectivity.

tries.summary: Prefix tree for efficient string prefix queries. Powers autocomplete, word search, and XOR tricks.

segment-trees.summary: Answer range queries with point/range updates in O(log n). Fenwick tree is lighter for prefix-sum updates.

bit-manipulation.summary: XOR tricks for pairs/duplicates, bit masking for subsets, power-of-two checks.

math.summary: GCD/LCM, prime sieve, modular arithmetic, combinatorics (nCr mod p). Often combined with DP.

string-algorithms.summary: KMP for O(n) pattern matching, Rabin-Karp for rolling hash, Z-function for prefix matches.
